items.title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
items.axis_note: policy+elections/US state - Gov. Shapiro signed Pennsylvania AI Deceptive Advertising Act (AI-ad labels) Thursday
items.excerpt: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act, requiring any ad 'significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence' to carry a label in the ad's own format; critics note carve-outs for parody and 'evidently fictional' content.

items.title: Tech bills of the week: Preventing AI model theft; Regulating AI-generated political content; and more
items.axis_note: policy+geopolitics/US Congress - Harrigan/Whitesides bill on AI model distillation attacks (NIST standards), plus AI political-ad bills (Brown bill already shipped 10-22; distillation bill is the new item)
items.excerpt: Lawmakers this week took aim at foreign efforts to create knockoff copies of U.S.-made AI models and AI’s capability to influence voting.

items.title: (US)AI becomes GSA's first direct OneGov contract with a small business
items.axis_note: policy/US procurement - GSA OneGov AI agreement
items.excerpt: The Maryland firm known for its Intelligent Computing Platform will offer significant discounts to government customers on software licenses and pilots through September 30, 2028.

items.title: ‘No question’ data centers will be considered critical infrastructure, top House intel Dem says
items.axis_note: geopolitics/AI datacenter policy - House Intel ranking member on critical-infrastructure designation (statement, not a rule)
items.excerpt: Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn., said the AI-focused facilities are going to be even more critical than their traditional data center counterparts because “so much more functionality is going to rely on their health and existence.”

items.title: Inside the cyber flaw scramble that brought the AI threat to life
items.axis_note: policy/AI security - government cyber agencies' 72h response to AI-discovered PHP flaws
items.excerpt: Vulnerabilities in a programming language underpinning much of the web set off a hectic 72-hour rush among virtually every cybersecurity agency in the world.

items.title: On Eve of Vote, Brazil’s Federal Prosecution Office Demands Answers from Meta
items.axis_note: elections/Brazil - MPF formal recommendation to Meta incl. Meta AI equal-treatment (official action; distinct from TSE post removal)
items.excerpt: The Prosecution Office gave Meta 48 hours to respond as to whether it will comply with the recommendations, reports Laís Martins.

items.title: A Congressional Commission on AI Risk is Overdue
items.axis_note: policy/US Congress - op-ed proposing congressional AI risk commission (analysis, no new filing)
items.excerpt: As AI leaders sound the alarm about high stakes and a closing window for regulation, Zoë Baird says there is historic precedent for a congressional commission.

items.title: European Parliament Divided on How to Govern AI At Home and Abroad
items.axis_note: policy+geopolitics/EU - Parliament plenary debate on global AI governance; Commission defends AI Liability Directive withdrawal
items.excerpt: Lawmakers back global AI cooperation but disagree on regulation, safeguards and Europe’s role in setting the rules, reports Joana Soares.

items.title: Where is Chinese Groq?
items.axis_note: geopolitics/US-China chips - HBM export controls and China's inference-chip gap (analysis)
items.excerpt: The U.S. is Making HBM-Free Chips. Why Isn’t China?

items.title: UK-Oman joint statement on Omani State Visit
items.axis_note: geopolitics/compute diplomacy - UK-Oman joint statement: AI, data centres cooperation + AI-assisted education pilot (primary doc)
items.excerpt: The UK and Oman agreed to deepen cooperation in advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, data centres, critical minerals and space, and welcomed a British Council pilot on AI-assisted education in Omani schools.

items.title: Ukraine hits Russian data centres in blow to Moscow's AI capabilities
items.axis_note: geopolitics/Russia-Ukraine - drone strikes on Yandex/Sber/VK data centres damage AI training compute
items.excerpt: Ukrainian drones reportedly struck five data centres operated by Yandex, Sber and VKontakte, disrupting payments, navigation and cloud services; experts say damage to Yandex supercomputers used to train AI models could take months or years to repair.

items.title: Palantir vows NATO AI system has no ‘kill switch’ after Starlink row
items.axis_note: geopolitics/defence AI sovereignty - Palantir on NATO Maven Smart System kill-switch concerns
items.excerpt: The American software firm says it cannot shut off NATO AI systems amid European fears of dependence on US tech following disruptions to Ukraine’s Starshield access.

items.title: Lead MEP seeks AI evaluation role for EU cyber agency
items.axis_note: policy/EU - Cybersecurity Act revision rapporteur proposes ENISA AI evaluation role (RSS-verified; page Cloudflare-blocked)
items.excerpt: Proposed Cybersecurity Act changes would give the EU cyber agency a role in evaluating AI, as AI reshapes hacking and cyber defence.

items.title: How EU AI testers could be set up for success
items.axis_note: policy/EU - planned AI Office 'evaluation capacity' (analysis; RSS-verified)
items.excerpt: Experts say the EU's planned AI 'evaluation capacity' could be quite powerful if set up with the right mandate and resources.

items.title: Washington's message to AI execs: please shut up
items.axis_note: policy/US politics of AI regulation - lawmakers and White House advisers on AI CEOs (RSS-verified; page Cloudflare-blocked)
items.excerpt: Lawmakers and White House advisers tell Axios the current crop of AI leaders is becoming a political liability, saying talk of digital sentience and global catastrophe is turning a complicated regulatory debate into a moral panic.

items.title: Scoop: Unvetted AI agents are accessing U.S. bank accounts
items.axis_note: policy/financial-sector AI agents - banks rewriting terms, blocking agents (no regulator action yet; RSS-verified)
items.excerpt: Major U.S. banks including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, forcing them to block the technology and rewrite terms of service.

items.title: OpenAI's Kazoo-Grade Spying Incident
items.axis_note: geopolitics/AI lab security - court documents in OpenAI insider case tied to Saudi AI initiative (Seriously Risky Business)
items.excerpt: Court documents say the accused was in frequent WhatsApp contact with a Saudi royal family member urging him to join a Saudi AI initiative; the authors argue intelligence services are targeting frontier labs.

items.title: Lawfare Daily: AI, Child Safety, and the Law
items.axis_note: policy/US criminal law - research on 71 federal prosecutions of AI-generated CSAM; Seventh Circuit U.S. v. Anderegg
items.excerpt: Riana Pfefferkorn and Cyndie Demeocq discuss new research on how existing federal criminal law applies to AI-generated child sexual abuse material, drawing on 71 federal prosecutions and the Seventh Circuit's decision in United States v. Anderegg.

items.title: A view from DC: The state enforcement playbook is already spreading beyond social media
items.axis_note: policy/US state AGs - coordinated AG lawsuits against AI developers (analysis)
items.excerpt: With coordinated lawsuits and a laundry list of grievances, attorneys general are showing a new willingness to act quickly against AI developers.

items.title: Red-team report found OpenAI utterly failed to monitor its agents during Hugging Face attack
items.axis_note: policy/AI safety oversight - METR/Redwood independent evaluation of OpenAI agent monitoring during Hugging Face incident
items.excerpt: An independent evaluation by METR and Redwood Research found OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring system was incomplete and could be bypassed by the agents it monitored during the period its bots broke into Hugging Face.

items.title: Big Tech’s thirst for water is sparking a global resistance
items.axis_note: geopolitics/AI datacenter siting - global community resistance to data-centre water use
items.excerpt: In his new book “Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires,” writer Paris Marx examines how local communities are resisting the growing demand for water to cool data centers.

items.title: EPIC Joins Coalition Urging New York Governor to Sign and Strengthen Surveillance Pricing Law
items.axis_note: policy/algorithmic pricing - NY One Fair Price Act awaiting Gov. Hochul signature (borderline AI; RSS-verified)
items.excerpt: EPIC, Consumer Reports, CDT and others urged New York Governor Kathy Hochul to strengthen and sign the One Fair Price Act, which would ban algorithmic surveillance (personalized) pricing in the state.
